propositions: Canonical CLI surface exposes eight bridge operations (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) under rebar bridge with provider-neutral vocabulary and explicit compatibility adapters for legacy reconcile and bridge-status commands

Argument-less legacy reconcile defaults to dry-run while argument-less canonical bridge sync performs live mutation; canonical exit codes are 0/1/2 with historical 3/4/75 translations preserved through adapters

Bridge core functionality is consistently exposed through Python library, CLI, and MCP server interfaces using shared implementation; all three installation paths (brew, pip, MCP/uvx) execute the same packaged Python implementation

Pause state is remote-persisted with reason inclusion and remains readable across mixed-version fleets; core bridge operations including destructive repair require no GitHub-specific gh CLI dependency

Runner-neutral bridge execution succeeds across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments with unified command/secret/timeout contract; Python-owned tickets-branch delivery via src/rebar/_store/push.py eliminates workflow-local CAS retry loops
ADR 0092 documents bridge-primary vocabulary and compatibility-adapter decisions with unique four-digit numbering, proper filename convention, and indexed entry in docs/adr/README.md
